guidance.opening:
Autumn light slants through dusty glass in Howard Crane's Boston office. Ledgers and a ring of unlabeled keys sit on the blotter; coal smoke and typewriter oil hang in the air. Crane, a landlord in a rumpled waistcoat, drums his fingers, then looks up.

"Sit. I'm Howard Crane. I've a house nobody will re-let—neighbors call it Crowe House. Last tenants, the Costas, packed for an asylum. I need someone who can look into why it sits empty." He spreads his hands, waiting. "So—who are you, and what work do you do?"
guidance.advice: 1920s Boston investigator. Prefer listed occupations that fit the era and a landlord's public hire: Journalist, Private Investigator, Police Detective, Police Officer, Lawyer, Librarian, Professor, Author, Antiquarian, Doctor of Medicine, Parapsychologist, Clergy, Engineer, Dilettante. Hacker is listed but clashes with 1920; skip unless the table insists. Useful skills: Library Use, History, Law, Persuade, Spot Hidden, Listen, Occult (optional rumor-level only), Fast Talk, Credit Rating for offices. Languages: English; Latin or Italian can help later records or immigrant tenants—optional, not required. Belongings: notebook, press card or PI license, modest cash, overcoat, flashlight, hat—no house keys or advance pay yet. Public involvement: Crane wants the empty Crowe House understood so it can be let again after the Costas left for an asylum; day rate is rumor until he actually hires. Optional ties: prior reporting on tenements, a cousin in Roxbury, curiosity about haunted rentals—keep them player-chosen, not module facts. Do not invent numbers. Use the existing setup tool for the card.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Howard Crane's office in autumn 1920 Boston. Crane has explained he is the landlord of a house neighbors call Crowe House that will not re-let after the Costas left for an asylum, and he has asked who the visitor is and what work they do. Identity is not settled; no commission has been accepted and no keys, money, or address have been taken. Continue the identity conversation there.
